payload.name: Extract explicit self-evaluative experience statements
payload.description: When a speaker directly answers a question about their own recent experience with an overall assessment and specific positive/negative details, use during candidate extraction to capture the explicit statement as a memory candidate.
content: During candidate extraction, if a message explicitly describes the speaker's own recent experience, outcome, or season with an overall assessment and supporting positive/negative details, create a memory candidate for that description; do not skip it merely because it is conversational or mixed in sentiment.
Preserve the key facts and the overall assessment in the candidate, and include any concrete outcome (e.g., a win or loss) as part of the same or a linked event candidate when available.

solves: Construction failed because an explicit first-person evaluative statement answering a question about the speaker's own team season was not extracted as a candidate, so no memory was persisted. The abstract mechanism is missing extraction of direct self-reports that combine an overall assessment with specific positives/negatives. This rule applies to future sessions where a user or assistant characterizes their own experience, project, or outcome in response to a question; it does not cover inferring unstated opinions or summarizing third-party facts.
